newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds flat in tentative trade ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds flat in tentative trade ahead of data.

text.p: Irish bonds were broadly unchanged in tentative trade on Thursday in line with a global trend of wait-and-see ahead of key U.S. non-farm payroll data due Friday, dealers said.

"We've seen some nervous price action today and not much flow," a dealer said. "Like everywhere else the policy is to wait for the payroll figures out of the U.S. in order to gauge the chances of another interest rate rise."
The data, expected at 1330 GMT on Friday, may show signs of inflation and, if strong, give clues to the likelihood of further rate hikes by the Federal Reserve to rein in the economy.

Despite the lack of trade flow on Thursday, the Irish market was outperforming both Germany and the UK by one or two basis points across the curve, one dealer said. "Although today that's not saying much."

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down two pence from Wednesday's close at 101.03 to yield 6.22 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was unchanged from the close at 107.05 to yield 6.95 percent.
Dealers said that little market reaction was expected to two key domestic data releases - Central Bank credit statistics, and EBR figures - due later in the afternoon.
"The banking statistics will be examined closely but as they have no direct interest rate repercussions they have little market-moving effect," a dealer said.
"Unless, that is, they are strongly above or below expectations. The EBR data will just give us an idea of how the economy's doing."
Very strong figures would have a negative impact on the bonds market.

"I'd be surprised if there is reaction to any of this today," a dealer said. "The market will probably wait until tomorrow to absorb the information, and quite possibly until after the U.S. payroll figures before doing anything." -- Kevin Smith, Dublin newsroom + 353 1 661 3377
